name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Biceps Curl
description:
Hold the kettlebell by the handle with the bell facing downward and curl it toward your shoulder by bending your elbow. Control the movement throughout the exercise, especially during the lowering phase.

This exercise develops biceps and forearm strength, as well as grip strength.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Two-Hand Kettlebell Upright Row
description:
Hold the kettlebell with both hands in front of you and pull it upward toward your chin. Do not raise your elbows above shoulder level.

This exercise develops shoulder strength and movement control.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Kettlebell Halo
description:
Hold the kettlebell in front of you and smoothly rotate it around your head in both directions. Keep your body stable and maintain control throughout the movement.

This exercise develops shoulder mobility and stability, movement control, and coordination.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Two-Hand Kettlebell Overhead Raise
description:
Hold the kettlebell with both hands at upper chest level and smoothly raise it overhead. Control the movement and avoid swinging or using momentum.

This exercise develops shoulder strength and movement control.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Bent-Over Kettlebell Row for the Rear Deltoid
description:
Bend your torso forward while keeping your back stable. As you exhale, smoothly raise your elbow up and out to the side to emphasize the rear deltoid.

Control the movement and avoid using momentum.

This exercise develops rear delt and shoulder strength, as well as movement control.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Bent-Over Kettlebell Rear Delt Fly
description:
Bend your torso forward while keeping your back stable. As you exhale, smoothly move the kettlebell out to the side while keeping your elbow fixed.

Control the movement and avoid using momentum.

This exercise develops rear delt and shoulder strength, as well as movement control.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Biceps Curl (Variation 2)
description:
Hold the kettlebell by the handle with the bell facing downward and curl it toward your shoulder by bending your elbow. Control the movement throughout the exercise, especially during the lowering phase.

This exercise develops biceps and forearm strength, as well as grip strength.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Curl
description:
Hold the kettlebell by the handle with the bell facing upward and curl it toward your shoulder by bending your elbow. Keep your wrist straight throughout the exercise — do not let it flex forward or backward.

Control the movement of the kettlebell, especially during the lowering phase.

This exercise develops biceps and forearm strength, wrist stability, and grip strength.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Biceps Curl
description:
Hold the kettlebell in one hand and curl it toward your shoulder by bending your elbow. Keep your elbow stable and avoid swinging your body. Control the kettlebell throughout the entire movement.

This exercise develops biceps and forearm strength, as well as grip strength.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Kettlebell Wrist Rotation
description:
Hold the kettlebell in front of your chest with the bell facing toward you. Smoothly rotate the kettlebell so the bell faces away from you, then return it to the starting position. Perform the movement primarily by rotating your wrists while keeping your elbows and torso stable.

This exercise develops forearm strength, wrist stability, and grip strength.

Recommended: 6–10 rotations in both directions, 4–5 sets.

name: Kettlebell Forearm and Wrist Raise
description:
Hold the kettlebell by the handle and smoothly raise it by bending your elbows about halfway through the range of motion. At the top of the movement, additionally flex your wrists.

Focus on gripping the kettlebell with your hands and engaging your forearms.

This exercise develops forearm, wrist, and grip strength.

Recommended: 8–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Overhead Kettlebell Triceps Extension
description:
Hold the kettlebell behind your head with your elbows bent. Smoothly extend your arms to raise the kettlebell upward, then lower it back behind your head in a controlled manner.

Keep your elbows stable and avoid using body momentum.

This exercise develops triceps strength and movement control.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Lying Kettlebell Triceps Extension
description:
Lie on your back and hold the kettlebell in front of your face. By bending your elbows, smoothly lower the kettlebell toward your forehead, then extend your arms to return it to the starting position.

Keep your elbows stable and maintain control throughout the movement.

This exercise develops triceps strength and elbow joint stability.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Push-Ups
description:
Get into a plank position with your hands about shoulder-width apart. Lower your body by bending your elbows, then smoothly push yourself back up. Keep your torso stable and avoid arching your lower back.

This exercise develops chest, triceps, and shoulder strength, as well as core stability.

Recommended: perform the maximum number of reps with proper form, 4–5 sets.

name: Push-Ups with One Hand on a Kettlebell
description:
Get into a plank position with one hand on the kettlebell bell and the other on the floor. Perform the push-up while keeping your torso stable.

The hand on the kettlebell gets a greater range of motion, stretching the chest muscle more deeply.

This exercise develops chest, triceps, and shoulder strength, as well as core stability and coordination.

Recommended: perform the maximum number of reps on each arm, 2–3 sets per arm.

name: Kettlebell Bench Press
description:
Lie on your back and hold the kettlebell in front of your chest. Smoothly lower the kettlebell to your chest, then press it back up. Control the movement and avoid using momentum.

A narrow hand position increases the load on the triceps while the chest muscles remain actively engaged.

This exercise develops chest, triceps, and shoulder strength.

Recommended: 10–12 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Bent-Over Kettlebell Row to the Waist
description:
Bend your torso forward while keeping your back stable, and row the kettlebell to your waist with both hands. You can use three grip variations: by the side handle, overhand, or underhand.

Control the movement and focus on feeling your back muscles working while squeezing your shoulder blades together.

This exercise develops back, arm, and forearm strength.

Recommended: 8–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: One-Arm Bent-Over Kettlebell Row
description:
Bend your torso forward while keeping your back stable, and row the kettlebell to your waist with one hand. You can perform the exercise without support or by bracing your free hand against a stable surface.

Control the movement and avoid using body momentum.

This exercise develops back, arm, and forearm strength.

Recommended: 6–10 reps per arm, 3–4 sets per arm.

name: Kettlebell Around-the-Body Rotation
description:
Keep your back straight and smoothly pass the kettlebell behind your body, transferring it from one hand to the other. Continue the circular motion around your body, controlling each handoff.

This exercise develops grip, forearm, and shoulder strength, as well as coordination and movement control.

Recommended: 8–10 rotations in each direction, 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Rotation
description:
Hold the kettlebell with both hands and perform a continuous circular motion: behind your head, down, in front of your body, and back behind your head.

Keep your torso stable and maintain control throughout the entire exercise.

This exercise develops shoulder, forearm, and grip strength and endurance, as well as coordination.

Recommended: 6–10 rotations in each direction, 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Side Swings
description:
Hold the kettlebell with both hands and perform smooth side-to-side swings, accompanied by torso rotation and weight transfer from one leg to the other.

Try to engage your whole body, coordinating the movement of your legs, torso, and arms.

This exercise develops full-body strength and coordination.

Recommended: 6–10 rotations to each side, 3–4 sets.

name: Russian Twists with a Kettlebell
description:
Sit on the floor, bend your knees, and lean your torso back slightly while keeping your back stable. Hold the kettlebell with both hands in front of your body and perform controlled rotations to the right and left, moving the kettlebell along with your torso.

This exercise develops core strength and endurance, especially in the oblique abdominal muscles.

Recommended: 8–20 rotations to each side, 3–4 sets.

name: Goblet Squat
description:
Hold the kettlebell with both hands at chest level. Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and perform a squat by bending your knees and pushing your hips back.

Keep your back straight, hold the kettlebell close to your chest, and maintain control of the movement.

This exercise develops leg and glute strength, as well as core stability.

Recommended: 8–14 reps in 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Sumo Squat
description:
Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width, toes pointed slightly outward. Hold the kettlebell with both hands in front of you between your legs. Perform a squat by bending your knees and lowering your hips while keeping your back straight.

This exercise develops glute, leg, and inner thigh strength.

Recommended: 8–14 reps in 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Reverse Lunges
description:
Hold the kettlebell and take a step back with one leg, lowering the back knee toward the floor. Keep your torso stable and return to the starting position in a controlled manner, then repeat the movement with the other leg while switching the kettlebell to the other hand.

This exercise develops leg and glute strength, balance, and coordination.

Recommended: 8–12 reps on each leg, 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
description:
Hold the kettlebell with both hands in front of you. Push your hips back, bend your knees slightly, and hinge your torso forward while keeping your back straight. Lower the kettlebell along your legs, then smoothly extend your hips and return to the starting position.

This exercise develops glute, hamstring, and back strength.

Recommended: 8–12 reps in 3–4 sets.

name: Lunges
description:
Hold the kettlebell in one hand and assume a lunge position with one leg forward. Smoothly lower your back knee toward the floor, then return to the lunge position without switching legs.

Complete the required number of repetitions on one leg, then switch legs.

This exercise develops leg and glute strength, balance, and coordination.

Recommended: 8–12 reps on each leg, 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Swings
description:
Hold the kettlebell with both hands and swing it between your legs by pushing your hips back. Then powerfully extend your hips and straighten your torso, driving the kettlebell forward to about chest height.

The primary movement comes from your legs and hips — your arms stay relaxed and simply guide the kettlebell.

This exercise develops explosive power and strength in the glutes and hamstrings.

Recommended: 8–12 reps in 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Swings with Squat
description:
Hold the kettlebell with both hands and swing it between your legs by pushing your hips back. Then powerfully extend your hips while simultaneously driving the kettlebell forward and transitioning into a deep squat.

From the squat position, raise the kettlebell to about head height, then lower it back down.

This exercise develops explosive leg power, shoulder strength, and coordination.

Recommended: 8–12 reps in 3–4 sets.

name: Traps (Shrugs + Farmer's Walk)
description:
Lean your torso slightly forward while keeping your back straight. Raise your shoulders up, then smoothly lower them.

After the first set of shrugs, without lowering the kettlebell, lock your shoulders in the raised position and immediately transition into a farmer's walk for 20–40 seconds. After the walk, still without lowering the kettlebell, perform shrugs again.

This complex develops trap strength and endurance, grip and forearm strength, and shoulder and core stability.

Recommended: 8–14 shrugs, then a 20–40 second farmer's walk, then 6–14 more shrugs. 3 sets total.

name: Double Kettlebell Complex: Swing + Squat + Push Press
description:
Perform a swing using your hips and legs to drive the kettlebells upward and lock them at your shoulders. From this position, perform a squat while keeping your back straight.

Then powerfully extend your legs and push press the kettlebells overhead, fully extending your arms. Lower the kettlebells back to your shoulders and immediately transition into the next swing.

This complex exercise develops full-body strength and endurance, explosive leg power, shoulder strength, coordination, and grip strength.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 3–4 sets.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Forward Throw
description:
Assume a stable fighting stance and hold the kettlebell in one hand at your shoulder. Powerfully extend your arm forward, performing a throw, while simultaneously engaging your legs and core to transfer force.

After the throw, controllably return the kettlebell to your shoulder and repeat the movement.

This exercise develops explosive shoulder and arm strength, coordination, core stability, and the ability to transfer force from the lower body through the core to the arm.

Recommended: 10 throws per arm, 3–4 sets.

name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Side Throw
description:
Assume a stable standing position and hold the kettlebell in one hand in front of you. Perform a powerful throw to the side while simultaneously rotating your torso and pivoting your feet in the direction of movement.

After the throw, controllably return to the starting position.

This exercise develops explosive shoulder and arm strength, coordination, core stability, and the ability to transfer force from the lower body through the core to the arm.

Recommended: 10 throws in each direction, 3–4 sets.

name: Rotational Kettlebell Push Press
description:
Assume a stable fighting stance and hold the kettlebell in one hand at your shoulder, keeping your free hand in a protective position near your chin. Powerfully press the kettlebell overhead while simultaneously rotating your torso and pivoting your foot in the direction of movement.

After the press, controllably return the kettlebell to your shoulder while simultaneously returning your torso and leg to the starting position.

This exercise develops explosive shoulder and arm strength, coordination, core stability, and rotational power.

Recommended: 8–10 reps per side, 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Push Press from a Lunge
description:
Assume a stable fighting stance and perform a reverse lunge while keeping your free hand in a protective position near your chin. Then powerfully return to standing while simultaneously cleaning the kettlebell to your shoulder.

From this position, immediately perform a push press overhead, extending your arm while simultaneously engaging your core and back leg.

This exercise develops leg and shoulder strength and explosive power, coordination, balance, core stability, and grip strength.

Recommended: 8–10 reps per side, 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Halo with Torso Rotation
description:
Hold the kettlebell with both hands in front of you, bell facing up. Perform a circular motion with the kettlebell around your head, and after it passes behind your head, simultaneously rotate your torso and pivot your foot in the direction of movement.

Then return your torso and leg to the starting position while continuing the halo motion, and repeat the movement in the opposite direction.

This exercise develops shoulder strength and endurance, grip strength, rotational power and core stability, coordination, and movement control.

Recommended: 6–10 reps per side, 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Around-the-Body Rotation with Side Throw
description:
Take the kettlebell and begin rotating it around your body, transferring it from one hand to the other. After the kettlebell completes one rotation around your body, bring it to the side position and perform a throw to the side while simultaneously rotating your torso and engaging your legs to transfer force.

After the throw, continue the rotation around your body, performing a throw in the opposite direction.

This exercise develops explosive power, rotational core strength, coordination, and the ability to transfer force from the legs through the core to the upper body.

Recommended: 6–10 throws in each direction, 3–4 sets.

name: Double Kettlebell Complex №1
description:
Perform the complex with two kettlebells without resting between exercises. Rest only after completing a full round.

The exercises sequentially engage the chest, back, shoulders, arms, legs, and core, while developing strength, muscular endurance, coordination, and the ability to work the entire body as one system.

Complex composition:
1. Kettlebell Push-Ups
2. Bent-Over Double Kettlebell Row
3. Double Kettlebell Swings
4. Double Kettlebell Clean + Push Press
5. Double Kettlebell Front Squats

Weight Selection: Choose a kettlebell weight that allows you to perform 6–8 repetitions of each exercise with proper form. Gradually increase the number of repetitions. Once you can perform more than 10 repetitions in all exercises without losing proper form, increase the kettlebell weight and return to 6–8 repetitions.

Recommended: complete 4 rounds, resting 1–3 minutes between rounds, depending on your fitness level. Beginners can start with 6 repetitions.

name: Double Kettlebell Complex №2
description:
Perform the complex with two kettlebells, executing exercises sequentially without resting between them.

The complex is designed to develop strength, muscular endurance, explosive power, and full-body coordination. The chest, triceps, shoulder muscles, back muscles, glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings, and core are actively engaged.

Complex composition:
1. Kettlebell Push-Ups → Double Kettlebell Deadlift: 6–8 reps
2. Kettlebell Push-Ups → Bent-Over Double Kettlebell Row: 6–8 reps
3. Kettlebell Push-Ups → Double Kettlebell Swing Clean → Push Press: 6–8 reps
4. Double Kettlebell Front Squats: 6–8 reps

Recommended: complete 3 rounds, resting 2–3 minutes between rounds.

name: Double Kettlebell Complex №3
description:
Perform the complex without resting between exercises. Sequential execution allows you to simultaneously develop strength, muscular endurance, explosive power, and full-body coordination.

The chest, shoulders, back, legs, triceps, forearms, and core are actively engaged.

Complex composition:
1. Kettlebell Push-Ups: 5–8
2. Double Kettlebell Swings: 5–8
3. Double Kettlebell Push Press: 5–8
4. Double Kettlebell Squats: 5–8

Recommended: complete 3 rounds, resting 2–3 minutes between rounds.

name: Single Kettlebell Complex №1
description:
Perform the complex with one kettlebell without resting between exercises. After completing the complex, switch arms and repeat the sequence on the other side.

The complex is designed to develop strength, muscular endurance, coordination, movement control, and the ability to effectively transfer force from the legs and core to the upper body. The leg muscles, back muscles, shoulders, triceps, biceps, forearms, and core are actively engaged.

Complex composition:
1. One-Arm Bent-Over Kettlebell Row — 5–8 reps
2. Kettlebell Clean — 5–8 reps
3. Kettlebell Overhead Press — 5–8 reps
4. One-Arm Kettlebell High Pull → Clean → Push Press — 5–8 reps

Recommended: complete 3–4 rounds on both arms, resting 2–3 minutes between rounds.

name: Full-Body Barbell Complex
description:
Perform the complex with a barbell without resting between exercises. Sequentially execute barbell push-ups, deadlifts, bent-over rows, and a combination of clean, squat, and overhead press.

The complex is designed to develop strength, muscular endurance, explosive power, and full-body coordination. The chest muscles, back muscles, glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings, shoulders, triceps, forearms, and core are actively engaged.

Complex composition:
1. Barbell Push-Ups — 5 reps
2. Deadlift — 5 reps
3. Bent-Over Barbell Row — 5 reps
4. Barbell Clean → Squat → Overhead Press — 5 reps

Recommended: complete 4 rounds, resting 2–3 minutes between rounds. Choose a barbell weight that allows you to perform 5–6 reps of each exercise with proper form throughout all 4 rounds.

name: Barbell Complex No. 2
description:
Perform the complex with a barbell without resting between exercises. Each exercise begins with a barbell push-up, immediately followed by an additional strength movement.

The complex is designed to develop strength, muscular endurance, explosive power, and full-body coordination. The chest muscles, back muscles, glutes, leg muscles, shoulders, triceps, forearms, and core are actively engaged.

Complex composition:
1. Barbell Push-Ups → Bent-Over Barbell Row — 5 reps
2. Barbell Push-Ups → Deadlift — 5 reps
3. Barbell Push-Ups → Deadlift → Barbell Clean → Push Press — 5 reps

Recommended: complete 3 rounds, resting 2–3 minutes between rounds.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Press
description:
Hold the kettlebell at shoulder level and press it overhead while maintaining full control throughout the movement. The shoulders perform most of the work, while the core muscles help stabilize the body.

This exercise develops shoulder strength and movement control.

Recommended: 6–10 reps in 4–5 sets.

name: Kettlebell Plank Drag
description:
Assume a high plank position with your feet shoulder-width apart or slightly wider, and place the kettlebell beside your body. Keeping your core stable, use one hand to pull the kettlebell underneath your body and move it to the opposite side. Then repeat the movement with the other hand.

Try to minimize torso rotation and avoid shifting your hips from side to side. Control the movement throughout the entire exercise.

This exercise develops core strength and stability, shoulder-girdle and arm strength, as well as body coordination and control.

Recommended: 8–20 drags to each side in 3 sets.

name: Diagonal Arm and Leg Raise from a Supine Position
description:
Lie on your back with your arms and legs extended. Simultaneously raise one leg while reaching the opposite hand toward the foot of the raised leg. Then controllably return to the starting position and repeat the movement with the opposite arm and leg.

Throughout the entire exercise, keep your arms, head, and legs elevated without touching the floor. Perform the exercise smoothly and without sudden movements, focusing on lifting your torso using your abdominal muscles rather than momentum. Maintain control of the movement and keep your core engaged.

This exercise develops core strength and endurance, improves coordination, balance, and body control, and enhances the ability to coordinate upper- and lower-body movements simultaneously.

Recommended: 8–12 reps per side in 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Torso Rotation from a Kneeling Position
description:
Start in a kneeling position and hold the kettlebell with both hands in front of you. Stand up and step one leg forward into a half-lunge position while simultaneously rotating your torso toward the front leg, moving the kettlebell with your body.

Then return to the starting kneeling position and repeat the movement on the opposite side.

This exercise develops core strength and stability, rotational strength, coordination, balance, and hip mobility. It also teaches the body to engage the legs, hips, and core simultaneously, effectively transferring force between the lower and upper body.

Recommended: 6–10 reps per side in 3–4 sets.

name: Kettlebell Swings with a Turn
description:
If you have never performed kettlebell swings before, go to the Exercises section and start by learning the basic kettlebell swing.

Hold the kettlebell with both hands and assume a stable stance. Push your hips back, slightly bending your knees, and swing the kettlebell between your legs. Then explosively extend your hips and torso, swinging the kettlebell upward and overhead. Once the kettlebell reaches the top position, rotate your torso and pivot your feet, turning your whole body.

Bring the kettlebell back down between your legs under control and continue the movement, alternating turns. Perform the exercise with coordinated movements, using the power of your legs and hips to generate momentum. Maintain control of the kettlebell and a stable torso. Do not try to lift the kettlebell overhead using only your arms.

This exercise develops explosive leg power, coordination, rotational core strength, balance, and the ability of the body to work as an integrated unit.

Recommended: 10–16 turns in total (5–8 per side) in 3 sets.

name: Kettlebell Explosive Squat Pull
description:
Lower into a squat, leaning your torso forward and holding the kettlebell between your legs. Then explosively extend your legs and hips, using their power to initiate the movement, and pull the kettlebell upward along your body. Keep your lower back straight during the pull.

At the top, the kettlebell should reach approximately upper-chest height (you can also pull it to around lower-chest height). Then lower the kettlebell under control and return to the squat position for the next repetition.

Try to initiate the movement by extending your legs and hips, using your arms to finish the pull. Maintain control of the kettlebell and avoid jerking it upward using only your arms.

This exercise develops explosive leg power, strengthens the shoulders and trapezius, improves coordination, and enhances the ability to transfer force from the lower body to the upper body.

Recommended: 10 reps in 3 sets.

name: Barbell Complex № 3
description:
Perform the complex with a barbell without resting between exercises. This complex is designed to improve overall physical fitness, strength endurance, explosive power, and coordination. It combines pushing and pulling movements.

Complex composition:
1. Push-Ups + Deadlift — 5 reps
2. Bent-Over Barbell Row — 5 reps
3. Barbell Clean — 5 reps
4. Overhead Barbell Press — 5 reps
5. Barbell Squat — 5 reps

Recommended: complete 4 rounds, resting 2–3 minutes between rounds. Choose a barbell weight that allows you to perform at least 5 repetitions of each exercise with proper technique throughout all rounds.

name: Double Kettlebell Complex №4
description:
Perform the complex with two kettlebells without resting between exercises. Performing the movements consecutively develops strength, explosive power, muscular endurance, and coordination.

The complex helps improve the ability to transfer force between the lower and upper body, as well as overall physical fitness. The back, shoulders, arms, legs, and core are actively engaged.

Complex composition:
1. Double Kettlebell Bent-Over Row — 5 reps
2. Double Kettlebell Clean — 5 reps
3. Double Kettlebell Clean → Squat → Overhead Press — 5 reps
4. Double Kettlebell Swings — 5 reps

If 5 reps feels too easy, you can increase the number to 8.

Recommended: complete 3–4 rounds, resting 2–3 minutes between rounds. Choose a kettlebell weight that allows you to maintain proper technique throughout every exercise and every round.
